correctness.rationale: For every k>=3,L>=2, a depth-ordered blocker is cleared once on its first incomplete arm excursion, and each complete clear costs precisely twice its depth. All other complete arm excursions cost twice arm length. The unique final blocker arrival gives the first unicycle rotor state with the walker on its two-cycle, so the explicit entry formula is exact. Strict maximization over final arm and blocker count gives (L-1)((2k-1)L-1), with one extremizer per hub pointer. The bounded law of large numbers gives the fixed-L typical limit. Verified on 24,344 initial labelled states including period and equality cases using verify.py. No infinite inference from finite checking.

value.rationale: Finite deterministic graph exploration has known O(mD) global stabilization but lacks configuration-resolved clocks on an archetypal multi-arm tree. The theorem gives an exact *all-initialization* clock, a sharp worst case unique up to the hub phase, and a distinct law-of-large-numbers typical clock. It quantifies substantial gap between rare adversarial masks and random initial memory; its object and statistic are natural rather than arbitrary finite slices.
